set.subject: reasoning
set.title: Circular seating
set.stimulus:
Six persons, J, K, L, M, N and P, sit around a circular table facing the centre, not necessarily in the same order.

1. K sits second to the left of M.
2. K sits second to the right of J.
3. N sits to the immediate left of K.
4. J sits exactly opposite P.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Who sits to the immediate left of L?

steps: Start with clues 1, 2, 3 and 4: together they fix K, M, J, N and P. (On a round or square table, place the first person anywhere — only relative positions matter.)
L takes the only seat left.
Final arrangement, clockwise from M: M, P, K, N, J, L.
L faces the centre, so L's right runs anticlockwise and left runs clockwise.
Immediately to the left of L: M — answer **M**.
solution.shortcut: Facing the centre: right = anticlockwise. Facing outside: right = clockwise. Fix the direction first, then count seats.
solution.trap: J is immediately to the right — counting in the wrong direction gives this option.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Who sits to the immediate right of N?

steps: Start with clues 1, 2, 3 and 4: together they fix K, M, J, N and P. (On a round or square table, place the first person anywhere — only relative positions matter.)
L takes the only seat left.
Final arrangement, clockwise from M: M, P, K, N, J, L.
N faces the centre, so N's right runs anticlockwise and left runs clockwise.
Immediately to the right of N: K — answer **K**.
solution.shortcut: Facing the centre: right = anticlockwise. Facing outside: right = clockwise. Fix the direction first, then count seats.
solution.trap: J is immediately to the left — counting in the wrong direction gives this option.

questions.prompt: Who are the immediate neighbours of K?

steps: Start with clues 1, 2, 3 and 4: together they fix K, M, J, N and P. (On a round or square table, place the first person anywhere — only relative positions matter.)
L takes the only seat left.
Final arrangement, clockwise from M: M, P, K, N, J, L.
On either side of K sit N and P — **N and P**.
solution.shortcut: Read the two seats next to the person straight off the final diagram.
solution.trap: J and M sit second to the left and right, not immediately next.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: How many persons sit between M and J when counted from the left of M?

steps: Start with clues 1, 2, 3 and 4: together they fix K, M, J, N and P. (On a round or square table, place the first person anywhere — only relative positions matter.)
L takes the only seat left.
Final arrangement, clockwise from M: M, P, K, N, J, L.
M faces the centre, so M's right runs anticlockwise and left runs clockwise.
Going from M towards M's left until J: P, K, N — **Three**.
solution.shortcut: Count only along the side the question names; the other arc gives a different number.
solution.trap: One is the count along the other side of the table.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Four of the following five pairs are alike in a certain way based on the given arrangement and so form a group. Which pair does not belong to that group?

steps: Start with clues 1, 2, 3 and 4: together they fix K, M, J, N and P. (On a round or square table, place the first person anywhere — only relative positions matter.)
L takes the only seat left.
Final arrangement, clockwise from M: M, P, K, N, J, L.
In "K, M", "N, P", "J, K" and "M, J", the second person sits second to the right of the first.
In "L, K", K sits elsewhere relative to L — so **L, K** is the odd one.
solution.shortcut: Find the relation in the first two pairs (same direction, same count), then test the rest.
solution.trap: Check direction from the first person’s own facing — a pair that is the same distance but on the other side does not belong.

Six persons, Bala, Chetan, Ishaan, Meera, Nitin and Vidya, sit around a circular table facing the centre, not necessarily in the same order.

1. Ishaan sits to the immediate right of Vidya.
2. Chetan sits second to the right of Ishaan.
3. Nitin sits to the immediate left of Chetan.
4. Chetan sits second to the left of Bala.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Who sits to the immediate left of Chetan?

steps: Start with clues 1, 2, 3 and 4: together they fix Ishaan, Vidya, Chetan, Nitin and Bala. (On a round or square table, place the first person anywhere — only relative positions matter.)
Meera takes the only seat left.
Final arrangement, clockwise from Vidya: Vidya, Bala, Meera, Chetan, Nitin, Ishaan.
Chetan faces the centre, so Chetan's right runs anticlockwise and left runs clockwise.
Immediately to the left of Chetan: Nitin — answer **Nitin**.
solution.shortcut: Facing the centre: right = anticlockwise. Facing outside: right = clockwise. Fix the direction first, then count seats.
solution.trap: Meera is immediately to the right — counting in the wrong direction gives this option.

steps: Start with clues 1, 2, 3 and 4: together they fix Ishaan, Vidya, Chetan, Nitin and Bala. (On a round or square table, place the first person anywhere — only relative positions matter.)

Final arrangement, clockwise from Vidya: Vidya, Bala, Meera, Chetan, Nitin, Ishaan.
Nitin faces the centre, so Nitin's right runs anticlockwise and left runs clockwise.
Second to the right of Nitin: Chetan → Meera — answer **Meera**.
solution.shortcut: Facing the centre: right = anticlockwise. Facing outside: right = clockwise. Fix the direction first, then count seats.
solution.trap: Vidya is second to the left — counting in the wrong direction gives this option.

Meera takes the only seat left.

Chetan faces the centre, so Chetan's right runs anticlockwise and left runs clockwise.

solution.shortcut: Count only along the side the question names; the other arc gives a different number.
solution.trap: None is the count along the other side of the table.

steps: Start with clues 1, 2, 3 and 4: together they fix Ishaan, Vidya, Chetan, Nitin and Bala. (On a round or square table, place the first person anywhere — only relative positions matter.)

steps: Start with clues 1, 2, 3 and 4: together they fix Q, T, R, S and P. (On a round or square table, place the first person anywhere — only relative positions matter.)
U takes the only seat left.
Final arrangement, clockwise from T: T, Q, U, P, R, S.
On either side of R sit S and P — **P and S**.
solution.shortcut: Read the two seats next to the person straight off the final diagram.
solution.trap: T and U sit second to the left and right, not immediately next.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: How many persons sit between R and U when counted from the left of R?

steps: Start with clues 1, 2, 3 and 4: together they fix Q, T, R, S and P. (On a round or square table, place the first person anywhere — only relative positions matter.)
U takes the only seat left.
Final arrangement, clockwise from T: T, Q, U, P, R, S.
R faces the centre, so R's right runs anticlockwise and left runs clockwise.
Going from R towards R's left until U: S, T, Q — **Three**.
solution.shortcut: Count only along the side the question names; the other arc gives a different number.
solution.trap: One is the count along the other side of the table.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: What is the position of P with respect to S?

steps: Start with clues 1, 2, 3 and 4: together they fix Q, T, R, S and P. (On a round or square table, place the first person anywhere — only relative positions matter.)
U takes the only seat left.
Final arrangement, clockwise from T: T, Q, U, P, R, S.
S faces the centre, so S's right runs anticlockwise and left runs clockwise.
From S, going to S's right: R → P — **Second to the right**.
solution.shortcut: Stand in the seat of the second person, face where they face, and count.
solution.trap: Second to the left is what you get by taking left/right from your own view instead of S's.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Four of the following five pairs are alike in a certain way based on the given arrangement and so form a group. Which pair does not belong to that group?

steps: Start with clues 1, 2, 3 and 4: together they fix Q, T, R, S and P. (On a round or square table, place the first person anywhere — only relative positions matter.)
U takes the only seat left.
Final arrangement, clockwise from T: T, Q, U, P, R, S.
In "U, R", "P, S", "R, T" and "T, U", the second person sits second to the left of the first.
In "S, T", T sits to the immediate left of S — so **S, T** is the odd one.
solution.shortcut: Find the relation in the first two pairs (same direction, same count), then test the rest.
solution.trap: Check direction from the first person’s own facing — a pair that is the same distance but on the other side does not belong.

set.subject: reasoning
set.title: Circular seating
set.stimulus:
Six persons, Q, R, S, T, U and V, sit around a circular table facing the centre, not necessarily in the same order.

1. T sits to the immediate left of V.
2. Q sits to the immediate right of U.
3. U sits second to the right of V.
4. S sits second to the right of U.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Who sits second to the right of Q?

steps: Start with clues 1, 3, 2 and 4: together they fix T, V, U, Q and S. (On a round or square table, place the first person anywhere — only relative positions matter.)
R takes the only seat left.
Final arrangement, clockwise from V: V, T, S, Q, U, R.
Q faces the centre, so Q's right runs anticlockwise and left runs clockwise.
Second to the right of Q: S → T — answer **T**.
solution.shortcut: Facing the centre: right = anticlockwise. Facing outside: right = clockwise. Fix the direction first, then count seats.
solution.trap: R is second to the left — counting in the wrong direction gives this option.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true according to the given arrangement?
options: Mohan is an immediate neighbour of Harish
Zubin is an immediate neighbour of Farida
Tejas is not an immediate neighbour of Zubin

steps: Start with clues 1, 2, 3 and 4: together they fix Harish, Tejas, Mohan, Pooja and Zubin. (On a round or square table, place the first person anywhere — only relative positions matter.)
Farida takes the only seat left.
Final arrangement, clockwise from Harish: Harish, Tejas, Mohan, Zubin, Pooja, Farida.
(A) Mohan is an immediate neighbour of Harish — false.
(B) Zubin is an immediate neighbour of Farida — false.
(C) Tejas is not an immediate neighbour of Zubin — **true**.
(D) Mohan sits exactly opposite Harish — false.
(E) Tejas sits exactly opposite Farida — false.
solution.shortcut: Test each statement on the final diagram, not on the clue list.
solution.trap: A statement copied from a clue with one word changed (left ↔ right, second ↔ third) looks familiar but is wrong.
